comment: The shared cases of the header-block rule. THREE readers use this file.
backend/ports_test.go runs each case through parseHeaderBlock, the Go
authority. header.test.js runs each case through the REAL JavaScript of
omn-go-editor.js. The two must answer the same offset.
bodyOffset is the byte index where the body starts. The editor puts the
caret there, and the server reads content[bodyOffset:] as the body.
It is a BYTE offset, because the Go side counts bytes. Each case below
is ASCII, thus a JavaScript string index answers the same number. A case
with a non-ASCII character in the header would need a byte count on the
JavaScript side, and none of these has one.
26.09.14 repaired a pair that had already moved apart, and four of eight
shapes disagreed. Add a case here when you find another shape.

a blank line inside the body
